dimensions.assessment: Affects juveniles subject to federal delinquency adjudication, prosecution, and incarceration, as well as state child welfare and juvenile justice agencies.
dimensions.evidence: children under eighteen years of age who are subject to adjudication, prosecution, and incarceration by the Federal Government

dimensions.assessment: Substantially modifies legal procedures, age thresholds, transfer rules, and murder culpability criteria for juvenile offenders.
dimensions.evidence: A person who was under the age of 18 at the time of the perpetration... is liable for murder only if one of the following is proven

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes competitive grant funding for state child welfare and juvenile justice collaboration carved from existing title IV-B funds and requires statistical reports.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary may award competitive grants jointly to a State child welfare agency and a State juvenile justice agency

dimensions.assessment: Amends title 18 and title 18/4 of the Social Security Act and United States Code, affecting federal criminal law, juvenile procedures, and social services grants.
dimensions.evidence: To amend title 18, United States Code, to account for the age of certain juvenile offenders and to amend title IV of the Social Security Act

dimensions.assessment: Permanent amendments to federal criminal and social security statutes, alongside recurring reporting requirements.

missing_information: Exact dollar amounts allocated for the competitive state grants from title IV-B funds are not specified.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill alters federal juvenile justice laws by changing age thresholds for delinquency proceedings and transfer to district courts, modifying murder liability for individuals under 18, requiring Bureau of Justice Statistics reports, and authorizing competitive grants to enhance collaboration between state child welfare and juvenile justice systems.
